title: The Drowned Sigil Again
premise: When the valley's ancient wards collapse and the stars go dark, mercenary Ines Sandoval discovers her silent god was never dead — it was imprisoned inside King Aldric, whose crown has been worn by a usurping entity for a decade. Ines and the ragtag found family she gathers — a ward-scholar, a deserter knight, and a boy who remembers being drowned — must carry the god's broken sigil to the capital and unbind king from crown before the usurper's armies raze the free cities. The ending demands a price: the sigil can only be reforged from a memory freely surrendered, and Ines gives up her recollection of the valley itself, freeing Aldric and restoring light to the sky at the cost of ever knowing where she came from.
about_author: Quentin Ashgrove is the pen name of a former river-cartographer who spent a decade mapping floodplains before turning to fiction. They write fantasy obsessed with borders, water, and the things people trade away to belong somewhere.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Ines Sandoval, patrolling the valley border for a god that hasn't spoken in ten years, watches the wards shatter and the sky go black. A wounded stranger stumbles through carrying a shattered silver sigil. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: dread and a strange, unwelcome relief that her exile is finally over.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Keeping
chapters.summary: Ward-scholar Odile deciphers the fallen wards: they didn't keep magic out of the valley — they kept something in, or someone asleep. The stranger dies whispering the name Aldric. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: scholarly certainty cracking into fear as she realizes her life's work served a lie.

chapters.title: A Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Ines recruits deserter knight Bramwell and meets Tam, an orphan who claims memories of drowning in another body. The group flees valley refugees and the first outriders of the usurper's army. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness — she swore off leading anyone, yet here they are.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the River
chapters.summary: Following the sigil's pull, they find a drowned shrine where Ines's god speaks for the first time in a decade — fragmented, pleading, revealing it was bound into the king's crown. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into grief, because Tam recognizes the binding ritual; he died under it once.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Crossing a burned province, the company shelters with free-city militia and learns the usurper's armies march on three cities at once. Bramwell faces his old commander and refuses to rejoin him. POV: Bramwell. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve — desertion becomes choice, not cowardice.

chapters.title: The Crown That Remembers
chapters.summary: Through Tam's drowned memories, the group witnesses the night of the binding: Aldric willingly took the god in to save his people, but the thing wearing his crown locked them both away. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: horror and compassion entwined — the enemy king may be the story's first victim.

chapters.title: Siege Lines
chapters.summary: Reaching the capital under cover of refugee columns, they infiltrate during the usurper's victory feast. Odile maps the crown-ward while Ines draws guards away; Bramwell is captured buying their time. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into focus — every calculation now carries lives.

chapters.title: Two Prisoners, One Throne
chapters.summary: Ines reaches the throne room and finds Aldric awake inside his own body, screaming behind the usurper's eyes. The god's voice threads through both of them. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fury meeting pity — she came to kill a tyrant and finds a man begging to be freed.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax: the reforged sigil requires a memory freely given. Tam offers his drowning; the god refuses — it must be a living memory of home. Ines surrenders the valley itself. The unbinding tears the usurper out of Aldric as the armies breach the walls. POV: alternating Ines and Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice as love made visible.

chapters.title: Where the Valley Used to Be
chapters.summary: The stars return; the armies break without their master. Aldric, freed but broken, abdicates toward the free cities' council. Ines stands at the valley's edge holding a map of a place she no longer remembers, surrounded by the family who remember it for her. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — justice outside the law, belonging beyond memory.
